newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt seeks delay in some sugar shipments - trader.
newsitem.headline: Egypt seeks delay in some sugar shipments - trader.

text.p: The Egyptian state's sugar refining company has asked its suppliers to delay some sugar shipments by several months because of a shortage of storage space, a Cairo-based sugar trader said on Friday.

But three or four vessels carrying about 20,000 tonnes each are already on their way and the trader, Hussam Nour of Otco, said he expected the state's Sugar and Integrated Industries Company (SIIC) to take delivery.
"They cannot default because they are government. I think they will solve the problem within a few days," he told Reuters.
Officials at the sugar company were not available because of the Egyptian weekend.
The vessels are carrying raw sugar mostly from Cuba -- part of the 750,000 tonnes the sugar refining company has ordered for delivery in stages through 1997, he added.

"They want to delay some cargoes for three or four months because they don't have room for storage but the vessels are on their way. No one knows why the sugar company booked cargoes for a year ahead. It's the first time they have done this," he said.
Nour is vice president of Otco, which acts as agent in Egypt for commodity traders Phibro.
